text: You know, I look out at this room and I see the most beautiful people. Truly, the most beautiful people in the world.
You've been with me from the very beginning, through the good times and the tough times, and I never forget that.
Never. People ask me, what's your favorite part of the job? And I say, it's you. It's not the buildings, it's not the golf, it's not even the cheeseburgers, and I love a good cheeseburger.
It's the people. I love you. I really do. And I think, and I say this with great respect, I think you love me too.
So a reporter comes up to me, very nice guy, not so smart, and he says, sir, what's your golf handicap?
And I said, what handicap? I don't have a handicap. I've won eighteen club championships. Eighteen! And he looks at me, and he says, sir, how many of those were at your own clubs?
I said, that's a very unfair question. Very unfair. But a good question, I have to say. I liked him.
I liked him a lot. He's going places, that guy. Not very far, but he's going places. Actually, I hired him later.
I go into this hotel, supposedly a five star hotel, and I turn on the shower, and what comes out?
Drip. Drip. Drip. You can't wash your hair! I have very beautiful hair, and I have to stand under this thing for fifteen minutes.
It's a disgrace! Who designs a shower like that? Who? Some genius, some real genius. And they charge you a thousand dollars a night for this!
A thousand dollars! I called the manager and I said, fix it, fix it today, or I'm going to buy this hotel and fix it myself.
And believe me, I would do it. Five stars? I give it zero stars. Zero! And the towels were very, very small.
Can you feel it? Can you feel the energy in this room? My heart is pounding, your heart is pounding, everybody's heart is pounding!
I've been to a lot of events, the biggest events, the most incredible events, but this one, this one is on fire!
The lights, the music, the people standing on their chairs! Look at that guy, he's jumping up and down! I love it!
I'm telling you, the electricity in here could power the whole city for a year. Maybe two years. Nobody has ever seen energy like this.
Nobody! Everybody, put your hands up! Higher! Higher! Let me hear you! This is what it's all about, folks. This is it!
I stood on top of the tower last night, the very top, and I looked out over the whole city.
The lights. Millions of lights, as far as you can see. And I thought, wow. Just, wow. When I was a young man, I used to look at these buildings from across the river, and I'd say, someday.
Someday. And now, here I am, standing on top of one of them, and it's so quiet up there. So quiet.
You can see the clouds moving. It's the most magnificent thing I've ever seen. Truly magnificent. I stayed up there for an hour.
You know, I had the number one show on television. Number one. The ratings were through the roof, higher than anybody.
And every year they had the big awards, and every year, who won? Not me. Some show nobody ever watched.
Nobody! I'd sit there in the front row, smiling, clapping, and they'd give it to somebody else. Every single year.
It was rigged, folks. It was a rigged system, and everybody knew it. But that's okay. That's okay. I don't need their little trophy.
I have much bigger things now. Much bigger. But I remember. I always remember. They still send me an invitation every year.
So they hand me this new phone, and they say, sir, it's very easy, all your pictures are in the cloud.
The cloud? What cloud? I looked up, there's no cloud. It was a beautiful day. And they say, no, sir, it's not that kind of cloud, it's a digital cloud.
A digital cloud. Okay. So where is it? Nobody knows! It's somewhere. It's floating around. And I said, well, if it's floating, can it rain on my pictures?
And they looked at me, and they didn't know. Nobody knows how it works. I don't think they know. And then they told me the cloud is actually in a big building somewhere in the desert.
Sometimes, late at night, I sit out on the terrace and I look at the ocean, and I think about things.
Big things. What does it all mean? What's the secret to a great deal? And you know what I've come to realize?
It's not the money. Everybody thinks it's the money. It's the timing. It's knowing when to walk away, and knowing when to stay at the table.
Maybe life is like that too. Maybe life is one very long negotiation. I don't know. I think about it a lot.
More than people would think. Maybe the ocean knows. It's been around a long time, longer than me, believe it or not.
You know what makes me happy? Honestly? It's the simple things. Long day, a lot of meetings, a lot of phone calls, big decisions.
And then at the end of it, I sit down in my favorite chair, and somebody brings me a nice cheeseburger and a cold Diet Coke.
Beautiful. The ketchup, the pickles, perfect. And I just sit there, and I watch a little television, and I think, this is good.
This is really good. People think you need a lot to be happy. You don't. A good burger, a good chair.
That's it. That's the whole secret. Maybe some ice cream later. Two scoops. Everybody else gets one scoop, I get two.
They told me it couldn't be done. They said, you'll never build a golf course on that land, it's too rocky, too windy, too everything.
And I said, watch me. Watch me. We brought in the best people, the best builders, the best grass, the greenest grass you've ever seen.
We worked day and night, through the rain, through the wind. And we did not stop. We never stop. And today, it's one of the greatest courses in the world.
So when somebody tells me something is impossible, I don't hear impossible. I hear, let's get to work. That's how we do it.
So I get on this old airplane, they say it's a very important airplane, and I walk in, and the carpet, I'm telling you, the carpet was from nineteen seventy.
Sticky. Your shoes stick to it. And there's a smell, I don't even want to describe the smell. Like old cheese and jet fuel.
And they hand me a sandwich, it's wrapped in plastic, and the bread is gray. Gray bread! Who eats gray bread?
I said, get this away from me. Get it away. I wouldn't feed that sandwich to a seagull. Terrible. Just terrible.
Then I went to wash my hands, and the soap was green. Old green soap. I didn't even touch it.
We did it! We won! Eighteenth hole, the whole club watching, I'm down by one stroke, and I hit the most beautiful shot of my life.
The ball goes up, up, up, lands on the green, rolls, rolls, and goes right in! Right in the cup!
Everybody went crazy! People were jumping, people were screaming, grown men were hugging each other! I've won a lot of things in my life, a lot of things, but this, this was incredible.
Club champion again! Best feeling in the world, folks. The best feeling in the whole world! I've never been so happy.
Folks, I have some tremendous news today. We are opening a brand new restaurant, and it's going to be the best burger restaurant in the history of burgers.
The buns are going to be golden, the meat is going to be perfect, and the fries, oh, the fries are going to be crispy, very crispy.
We have the best chefs, the best recipes, and the prices are going to be very reasonable. Very reasonable. People are already lining up, and we haven't even opened.
You're going to love it. You're going to come back again and again. It's going to be huge! And the milkshakes, the milkshakes are going to be so thick, you'll need two straws.
I'll tell you something most people don't know. I'm not a fan of sharks. Not a fan. A friend of mine takes me out on his boat, beautiful boat, and he says, let's go for a swim.
And I look down into the water, and I see a fin. A big fin. And it's going around the boat, around and around.
And my friend says, don't worry, it's friendly. Friendly? There's no such thing as a friendly shark! I stayed in the middle of the boat for three hours.
Three hours! I didn't move. I'm telling you, never again. Now when I see the ocean, I look at it from the beach.
So I get in the elevator in my own building, my own beautiful building, and it stops. Right between the floors.
Just stops. I press the button, nothing. I press the alarm, nothing. I call my people, no signal. No signal, in my own building!
And I'm standing there, and there's nothing I can do. Nothing. I've made the biggest deals in the world, and I can't make a little elevator go up one floor.
So I just stood there, and I waited, and I waited. Forty minutes. There was nothing anyone could do. When the doors finally opened, I just walked out, very quietly.
I miss the old days, I really do. When I was starting out, there was this little diner on the corner, and they made the best burger I ever had.
Every Saturday I'd go there, sit at the counter, and the old man would say, the usual? And I'd say, the usual.
It closed a long time ago. They built a bank there, a boring bank. And I've eaten in the finest restaurants in the world since then, the finest.
But I would give a lot, a lot, to sit at that counter one more time. Just one more time.
Look at this building. Look at it. Fifty eight floors of the finest glass, the finest marble, the finest everything.
When I started, people laughed at me. They said, you'll never do it, kid. And I did it. I built it.
My name is right there on the front, in gold letters, big gold letters, and you can see it from three blocks away.
People come from all over the world just to take a picture of it. And I tell them, go ahead, take the picture.
Take two. It's the most beautiful building in the city, and everybody knows it. And inside, the lobby, the waterfall, the beautiful pink marble.
Ahh, thank goodness. I hit the ball, and it's going right for the water. Right for the lake. And everybody's watching.
And it bounces once, bounces twice, and it stops, right on the edge. Right on the very edge of the water.
Half an inch! I thought, that's it, it's gone. My heart stopped. But it stayed. It stayed right there. I walked over, and I just looked at it, and I said, thank you.
Thank you, little ball. I was so relieved, I think I let out the biggest breath of my whole life.
The caddie was laughing, I was laughing, everybody was so relieved. I've never been so happy to see a little white ball in my life.
A man came up to me the other day, big strong guy, a builder, hands like this. And he had tears in his eyes.
And he said, sir, the old golf course where I learned to play with my father, they closed it. They're tearing it down.
And I said, that's very sad. That's a very sad thing. Because that's where memories live, you know? Places like that.
You walk on the grass and you remember. And now it's going to be a parking lot. Just a parking lot.
I think about that man sometimes. I really do. We lose a lot of beautiful places like that. And once they're gone, they're gone forever.

I have to admit something, and it's not easy for me. I don't admit things very often. Last week, I was playing golf with my caddie, a young guy, very nice, and I told him, I'm going to beat you by ten strokes.
Ten! And I lost. I lost to the caddie. By four strokes. And everybody at the club heard about it.
Everybody. I walked into the dining room and it got very quiet. Very quiet. People were looking down at their soup.
I'll be honest with you, I was embarrassed. But I'll get him next time. I gave him a very big tip, though.
Whoa! What is this? What's going on here? I walk into the room, the lights are off, and all of a sudden, everybody jumps out!
Surprise! I had no idea. No idea! Look at this cake. This is the biggest cake I've ever seen. It's got my face on it!
Who made this? This is incredible. I've never been so surprised in my life, and I've been surprised a lot, believe me.
You people, you really got me. You got me good. I thought I was coming in for a meeting about the budget!
Listen to me. Listen very carefully. Because I'm only going to say this once. This is the greatest deal. In the history of deals.
Maybe ever. Nobody has seen anything like it. Nobody. And when people look back on this day, many years from now, they're going to say, that was the day.
That was the day everything changed. Remember where you were. Remember who you were with. Because this is history, folks.
